summary: The ranking is right, but players think in brands and every brand owned by a top-10 group (Kia, Chevrolet, Jeep, Audi, Lexus) costs a life. Fix the brand mapping and it is a fair daily.
reasons: Casual run: Toyota, Ford, Honda, Volkswagen, GM, Hyundai (6/10), then Tesla, BMW, Mercedes, Nissan and Kia took all five lives. Kia should count toward Hyundai Motor Group (#3), not against the player.

'chevy' is autocorrected to Chery (#15) and 'chevrolet', 'jeep', 'dodge', 'chrysler', 'fiat', 'peugeot', 'audi', 'porsche', 'lexus', 'cadillac', 'volvo' all cost a life though their parent group is in the top 10. With 'groups' in the prompt this is the textbook fairness 1.
Values look right for 2025 (Toyota 11.3M, VW 9.0M, Hyundai 7.3M). Fan run is clean at 10/10 with Nissan (#13) as a good near miss.
fixes: Map brands to their parent group in scripts/intent.ts (or a brand table), so they count as that top-10 answer: Kia, Genesis -> Hyundai Motor Group; Chevrolet, Chevy, Cadillac, Buick, GMC -> General Motors; Jeep, Dodge, Ram, Chrysler, Fiat, Peugeot, Citroen, Opel, Vauxhall, Alfa Romeo, Maserati, Fiat Chrysler, FCA, PSA -> Stellantis; Audi, Porsche, Skoda, SEAT, Bentley, Lamborghini -> Volkswagen Group; Lexus, Daihatsu -> Toyota; Acura -> Honda; Volvo, Polestar, Lotus, Zeekr -> Geely; MG -> SAIC Motor; Lincoln -> Ford. At minimum make them free instead of costly.
'chevy' must not autocorrect to Chery (#15); add 'Chevy' as a known name (alias of the GM group per above, or of Chevrolet in the lexicon).

Rank the next groups with values instead of leaving them unranked with no stat: Renault Group (about 2.3M), BMW Group (about 2.5M), Mercedes-Benz Group (about 2.2M), Tesla (about 1.6M), Tata Motors, Great Wall, Dongfeng, Mazda, Mitsubishi, Subaru. Tesla, BMW and Mercedes are the most common casual guesses and the near-miss reveal should show their numbers. Ranks 11+ currently stop at #15 (Chery).
